outcome_detail: Settled March 3, 2026 in U.S. District Court (E.D. Ky.) as jury selection was about to begin. Plaintiff's counsel described two settlements: $300,000 from the Letcher County Sheriff's Office and an undisclosed amount from former deputy Ben Fields personally.
criminal_detail: Ben Fields pleaded guilty to third-degree rape, third-degree sodomy, second-degree perjury, and tampering with a prisoner monitoring device, and was sentenced in 2024 to six months in jail plus about six and a half years of probation; three charges involving a second alleged victim were dismissed after that woman died. Separately, then-Sheriff Shawn 'Mickey' Stines — a defendant in the civil suit for failure to train/supervise — was charged with murder in the September 19, 2024 shooting death of District Judge Kevin Mullins inside the same courthouse.
description: A woman on home incarceration filed a federal civil rights lawsuit in the Eastern District of Kentucky alleging that Letcher County deputy sheriff Ben Fields coerced her into sexual acts inside Judge Kevin Mullins' courthouse chambers over roughly six months from June 2021 through January 2022 in exchange for staying out of jail, and that the sheriff's office failed to train and supervise deputies on sexual misconduct despite recognizing it as a high-risk area. Fields pleaded guilty to third-degree rape, third-degree sodomy, second-degree perjury, and tampering with a prisoner monitoring device, and was sentenced in 2024 to six months in jail plus probation. In September 2025, a federal judge denied dismissal and ruled a jury should decide whether Fields coerced the plaintiff into sexual contact. On March 3, 2026, minutes before jury selection, the parties settled, with plaintiff's counsel reporting $300,000 from the sheriff's office and an undisclosed amount from Fields. Then-Sheriff Shawn 'Mickey' Stines, deposed in the suit days earlier, was separately charged with murdering Judge Mullins in September 2024.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (sheriff). Settlement amount is partially undisclosed: settlement_amount_original reflects only the disclosed $300,000 sheriff's-office portion; Fields' personal settlement amount was not disclosed. Early coverage described two women plaintiffs; the second alleged victim died before resolution, and settlement coverage concerns the surviving plaintiff's suit.
